cohorts.subjects: Living patients: 83 people who had a thoracic or abdominal CT on a GE LightSpeed VCT for abdominal or thoracic symptoms, with no spinal complaint, selected retrospectively from the PACS of the First Affiliated Hospital of Chongqing Medical University, Chongqing, China (the authors' hospital; Inference: the PACS is that hospital's). Excluded: marked osteophytes, significant vertebral degeneration, vertebral fracture, neoplasm of a vertebral body on CT, vertebrae visibly rotated axially relative to the scanner axis, columns with a large lateral slant. Split into four groups A1, A2, B1, B2 by age (over 40 or not) and sex, 22, 19, 21 and 21 people; which group is which is not stated. Ethnicity not stated (Inference: Chinese). Only the Table 5 columns headed Current report are this cohort's.
cohorts.n_units: 830 endplates (Table 1 n = 830), ten per person from T10 inferior to L3 superior; Male n = 430 and Female n = 400 in Tables 2 and 3 (Inference: endplate counts, so 43 men and 40 women)
cohorts.ages: mean 43 years, range 21-65; grouped as over 40 or not
cohorts.sexes: not stated in words; Inference from n = 430 and 400 endplates: 43 men, 40 women (22 + 21 and 19 + 21 fit the four groups)

No subjects: the conventional Cronbach alpha range regarded as satisfactory for inter-modality reliability (Bland and Altman [21]) and the authors' uncited statement that osteoporosis usually starts in the fourth decade of life.

techniques.instrument: GE LightSpeed VCT; all images multiplanar reformatted at 0.625 mm slice thickness; landmarks and measurements with the PACS's internal measuring tools. Figure overlays: 120 kV, 298 mA, SFOV 50.0 cm, 0.6 s, tilt 0.0, WW 1800 / WL 600.
techniques.how: Midsagittal plane (MSP): the image in which the whole contour of that vertebra's spinous process is seen. Specified coronal plane (SCP): the coronal plane through the most concave point Cm of the endplate on the MSP. On the MSP the anterior (A) and posterior (P) rims of the endplate and Cm are marked by hand; on the SCP the right (R) and left (L) rims and the most concave point Cs. SCA is the obtuse angle A-Cm-P; SD is the length of AP; C' is the foot of the perpendicular from Cm to AP and LCR is C'P / AP in percent; CCA is the angle R-Cs-L; TD is the length of RL. aSD is the mean of a vertebra's superior and inferior SD. Ten endplates, T10 inf to L3 sup. For the cadaver CT scans the same marking and measuring was done but only SCA and SD.
techniques.magnification: not applicable: lengths read in mm from CT with the PACS tool; in-plane pixel size not stated
techniques.observers: one trained user (initials CH) for the patients; for the cadaver CT not stated (Inference: the same); no intra- or inter-observer repeat reported

within_paper: Two cohorts of this paper's own, with no subjects in common as far as the paper states: the 83 living patients (Tables 1, 2, 3 and the Current report columns of Table 5) and the 10 cadaveric spines (Table 4), p. 1815 (PDF 2). Within the patients, every table is the same 83 people: Table 1 pools both sexes (n = 830 endplates), Tables 2, 3 and 5 split them by sex (n = 430 and 400), and the groups A1 to B2 partition them by age and sex, p. 1815 (PDF 2), p. 1817-1819 (PDF 4-6). Table 2's aSD is derived from the same SD values Table 5 gives per endplate (the mean of a vertebra's two endplates), and Table 5's transverse diameters repeat Table 3, p. 1816-1819 (PDF 3-6). The 10 cadaveric spines were measured twice, on their CT and on photographs of their midsagittal cuts, the same specimens and endplates by two methods (Table 4, n = 100), p. 1815-1816 (PDF 2-3), p. 1818 (PDF 5). Inference: the Figs. 2-3 example is one of the 83 patients, not stated.
